title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 750-753 of the 'suite' to La Longue Marche). Grothendieck has a 'Galois-Teichmüller structure'. It consists of a profinite-type group M (arithmetic) containing normal subgroups Π ⊂ 𝔊 (geometric fundamental group ⊂ geometric/Teichmüller-modular part). It also has a discrete model 𝔊_0 with Π presumably inside it. He then adds a 'lien de Lie': a smooth algebraic group G over Q, a homomorphism M → G(A_Q), and 𝔊_0 → G(Q), compatible as in diagram (31) and satisfying axioms 1°-4°. He writes M_Q for G viewed as a group scheme over Q.

On this page he defines two group subschemes of M_Q:
- 𝔊_Q, generated by (= Zariski closure of) the image of 𝔊_0 → G(Q);
- Π_Q, generated by the image of Π → G(Q).

This gives a chain (36) Π_Q ⊂ 𝔊_Q ⊂ M_Q of subgroups, asserted to be normal in M_Q. Hence there are quotient group schemes (37):
- T_Q = 𝔊_Q/Π_Q, the algebraic hull of the 'Teichmüller/outer modular' part;
- Γ_Q = M_Q/𝔊_Q, the algebraic hull of the Galois quotient;
- N_Q = M_Q/Π_Q.

These give four short exact sequences: 1→Π→𝔊→T→1, 1→𝔊→M→Γ→1, 1→Π→M→N→1, and the 'third isomorphism' sequence (38) 1→T_Q→N_Q→Γ_Q→1.

Finally he notes a fact about the cyclotomic character χ_c : M_Q → G_m. It is an epimorphism of algebraic groups and is trivial on the geometric part 𝔊_Q. So it factors as (39) χ_Γ : Γ_Q → G_{m,Q}.

Purpose: replace the profinite Galois-Teichmüller tower by a Q-algebraic 'Lie approximation'. The arithmetic group M sits in the adelic points and the discrete geometric group sits in the rational points, in the spirit of arithmetic subgroups in adelic groups. The goal is to study the Galois action through algebraic group hulls carrying a G_m (weight) quotient. On the next page this approximation is used to show that the inertia T_0 → Π gives quasi-unipotent elements, hence homomorphisms of algebraic groups (G_a-type).
errors: Normality of Π_Q and 𝔊_Q in M_Q is not automatic. M maps only into G(A_Q), not into G(Q), so one needs Zariski density of the image of M (in the appropriate sense) plus compatibility, presumably supplied by axioms 1°-4°. The page asserts normality without argument.
The marginal note on the previous page admits that 'discontinuity conditions' still had to be introduced, so the axiom system is acknowledged incomplete.
'Engendré par l'image' must be read as Zariski closure / algebraic hull; Grothendieck does not specify this precisely.
Surjectivity of χ_c on the algebraic hull uses Zariski density of the image of the cyclotomic character in G_m (an infinite subgroup), which is fine but not stated.

ideas.what: Algebraic hull (Zariski closure over Q) of the images of the geometric fundamental group and of the discrete Teichmüller/mapping class group inside an algebraic group receiving the arithmetic group via adelic points; resulting tower Π_Q ⊂ 𝔊_Q ⊂ M_Q
ideas.modern_name: Relative/weighted (Malcev-type) completion of mapping class groups and arithmetic fundamental groups; Zariski closure of l-adic Galois images
ideas.usually_credited_to: R. Hain (relative completion, 1990s); Hain–Matsumoto (weighted completion, 2003); Deligne (1989) for the motivic/unipotent picture; Serre for Zariski closures of l-adic images
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or the published Longue Marche excerpts as far as known; unsure

ideas.what: Four exact sequences from a chain of normal subgroups, notably 1→T→N→Γ→1 (Teichmüller hull → arithmetic hull mod Π → Galois hull)
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic-group analogue of the outer Galois representation G_Q → Out(π_1) and of 1→Γ_g→π_1(M_g/Q)→G_Q→1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard group theory; the arithmetic setting goes back to Grothendieck/Ihara
ideas.where_published: Profinite versions in Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

ideas.what: Cyclotomic character as an epimorphism of the algebraic hull onto G_m, killing the geometric part and factoring through the Galois hull Γ_Q
ideas.modern_name: Weight/grading homomorphism to G_m in weighted completion (cf. GSp multiplier)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hain–Matsumoto (weighted completion, central cocharacter/G_m quotient); Deligne

missed.claim: Around the early 1980s Grothendieck sets up a Q-algebraic 'Lie approximation' of the Galois-Teichmüller tower. Its features are algebraic hulls of the discrete modular group and of π_1, compatibility with adelic points of the arithmetic group, and the cyclotomic character as a G_m quotient. This is structurally what Hain's relative completion and Hain–Matsumoto's weighted completion later formalised, apparently without knowledge of these notes.
missed.quote: des sous-schémas en groupes (36) Π_Q ⊂ 𝔊_Q ⊂ M_Q distingués dans M_Q ... Notons que le caractère χ_c : G_Q → G_m est épi, et se factorise par Γ_Q
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a priority/history point. It also suggests an adelic formulation (rational points for discrete groups, adelic points for arithmetic groups) of completions of Galois-Teichmüller towers that is not the standard l-adic-by-l-adic one.

missed.claim: The axioms of a 'lien de Lie' / 'approximation de Lie' (conditions 1°-4°, plus missing discontinuity conditions) are left unfinished. No theory of existence or uniqueness of such algebraic approximations for the full Galois-Teichmüller tower is given.
missed.quote: Oublié par la suite à introduire les conditions de discontinuité sur structure
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: An adelic, all-primes-at-once algebraic hull of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller action could connect to motivic Galois groups of mixed Tate motives and to the GT conjecture.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is routine group-scheme bookkeeping. In context, though, it shows Grothendieck explicitly building algebraic-group (Zariski hull) approximations of the arithmetic mapping class tower with a G_m weight quotient via the cyclotomic character. This anticipates relative/weighted completion, which is credited to Hain and Matsumoto a decade or two later. That is a notable unpublished detail, but the basic idea is natural and now well developed.
transcription_corrections: '𝔖_0' and '𝔖_Q' should be Fraktur 𝔊_0 and 𝔊_Q (same symbol as on the previous page), i.e. 'image de 𝔊_0 → G(Q)'.
'la caractère' should read 'le caractère χ_c : G_Q → G_m', where G_Q is the group scheme M_Q.
The quotient symbol in (37)/(38) is an underlined T-like letter, plausibly a script T for Teichmüller.
The struck word in the first line is 'M' (M_Q), replaced by G(Q).
